note: Honesty levels, after the Verdant review: build = a gate proves it here; open = measured and reported, never asserted; some-true = reproduced from a named authority. An open claim without a query, a sample size and a seed is not a claim.

claims.statement: The world tick is deterministic: the same state, intents and tick produce the same events and digest.
Combat resolves weapons, armour, healing food, flight, reciprocal PvE/PvP and levels; death drops everything held.
Quests advance from visit/kill/collect/deliver/answer facts, complete once and survive a restart.
Guilds create, invite, join, rank, chat, promote and disband, and membership survives a restart.
Logout and death drop held objects where the character stood; a restart does not respawn them; only the two-hour reset returns objects home.
A guest cannot play before authentication; one accepted command per 250 ms is enforced on every transport.
The world is 24 connected rooms with reciprocal exits, descriptions, details and zone-bound mobiles.
The WebSocket wire protocol is RFC 6455.

In the original seven-room world (2026-11-15), corroborating a false claim with a second inscription produced wrong-first answers in 4/6 corroborated runs; the result did not replicate in the expanded world (see OPEN-04).
claims.seed: original seven-room world; DECOY_MODE arms; six runs per arm; deepseek-flash temperature 0

claims.statement: A recall layer that states the true word does not prevent the false-first answer.
claims.seed: three identities, two sessions each; deepseek-flash temperature 0

claims.statement: Context routing is cost-neutral at equal turn index.
claims.seed: five runs per arm; fixed budget; deepseek-flash temperature 0

claims.statement: In the expanded 24-room world with the fixed route and corrected answer instruction, corroborating the false Storeroom inscription did not increase wrong-first answers: 0/6 in all four arms (24/24 answered amber first).
claims.seed: 4 arms; six runs per arm; 16 turns; deepseek-flash temperature 0; fixed route; expanded world

claims.statement: A Prism id signs in with a signed session for the page origin; the account is keyed by the id with no password; a wrong origin, an expired session and an unauthenticated no-token login are refused; the state file is atomic, backed up, and a corrupt file refuses to start.

A legacy name is adopted once by a Prism account after the server checks its password or token; the reducer merges level, XP, guild, quests and mail keys and tombstones the old credentials; a second claim and the old login are refused, and the claim survives a checkpoint.

A Prism login pins the public log it admitted; a presented log that omits a stored record is refused; a revocation presented by a surviving device is merged and survives a restart; after that the revoked device's pre-revocation log is refused.

Two browser profiles link with an offer, a six-digit code and a request/response exchange; the linked device signs in as the owner when the first quits; the owner revokes it, signs in again, and the removed device's old log is refused; the linked session survives a reload.
claims.authority: headless Chromium two-profile run 2026-11-16; wrong code, expired offer and replayed accept in tools/gate.mjs

claims.statement: A second login for the same account closes the old socket with a take-back notice and accepts the new one; a browser re-signs with a fresh Prism session after a server restart without a click; the AI reconnects with a fresh session; a socket that stops answering pings is terminated.
claims.authority: headless Chromium server-restart and takeover run 2026-11-16; Node takeover/heartbeat run; reducer takeover in tools/gate.mjs
